# Welcome {.unnumbered}

![](images/crew.svg){.column-body-outset .hero fig-alt="An isometric ink drawing of cartoon elephants at work around a Postgres database. One sends jobs from a laptop onto a belt, one picks a job off the belt, one carries it up a ramp into a hatch on the database, one inspects the hatch with a magnifying glass, one repairs the database with a wrench, one wheels cubes of data away, one stacks them on a pile and one checks them off on a clipboard."}

Applications usually keep their rows in Postgres and send other work to separate systems, such as a
queue for background jobs, a vector store for semantic search, or a pipeline that copies changes to
an analytical database. This book shows how Postgres can do each of these jobs itself, how each one
works inside the database, and where it stops being a good fit.

## The map

![](images/world.svg){.column-body-outset .hero fig-alt="An isometric ink drawing of the book as a small world. A Postgres cylinder stands at the center of a plate, and five districts around it stand for Python, Search, Queues, Moving data, and Access and operations."}

::: {.map}
::: {}
**Postgres from Python**

How SQLAlchemy talks to Postgres in sync and async code, how JSONB stores documents next to typed
columns, what PgBouncer does for connections, and how PGlite runs Postgres inside a test process.
:::
::: {}
**Search**

How pgvector compares and indexes embeddings, how its HNSW index differs from DiskANN and PRISM, and
how to load and read vectors in bulk.
:::
::: {}
**Queues**

How pgqueuer runs a job queue in a table, and how pgmq builds a message queue on a visibility
timeout.
:::
::: {}
**Moving data**

How logical replication copies changes to a second Postgres, how Apache Doris follows Postgres with
its own CDC job, and how pg_ducklake keeps columnar tables inside Postgres.
:::
::: {}
**Access and operations**

How Pulumi and pgsesame keep roles and grants in code, and how the same servers run on local
Kubernetes.
:::
:::

## How to read it

Two chapters include a scene that replays a recorded run of the lab's app. In
[Chapter 1](chapters/sqlalchemy.qmd) it shows sync and async vector searches side by side, and in
[Chapter 8](chapters/pgqueuer.qmd) it shows workers sharing a queue table. Each scene plays as a
recording until you press Run it live. The pgvector, JSONB and pgmq chapters end with a SQL console
that runs Postgres in the page, and the appendix holds the notebooks behind the chapters, with
their outputs.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Run it yourself

Clone the repository, then run `cp .env.example .env`, `uv sync` and `just db` to start Postgres 16
with pgvector on `localhost:5432`. A few notebooks need another server, and
[Running the lab](chapters/running-the-lab.qmd) lists them.
:::
